items.front: In AWS edge services, users around the world load popular static images slowly from one S3 bucket. What do you put in front of the bucket?
items.extra: CloudFront is a good choice for [frequently accessed static content](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-good-for-static-edge-content) such as popular website images.

items.front: CloudFront or Global Accelerator: a game sends UDP traffic to two Regions, and partners need fixed IP addresses. Which one do you choose?
items.extra: Global Accelerator fits non-HTTP traffic such as [gaming (UDP), IoT (MQTT), or Voice over IP](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-good-fit-non-http-static-ip-fast-failover).

items.front: In CloudFront, users must not open files with S3 URLs. What do you attach to the S3 origin?
items.extra: With the bucket secured, users [cannot access it directly by using Amazon S3 URLs](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-private-s3-oac-plus-signed-urls).

items.front: In CloudFront, only paying users can download one installer file, for a limited time. What do you use?
items.extra: Signed URLs fit when you [restrict access to individual files](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-signed-url-when-individual-files-or-no-cookies).

items.front: In CloudFront, subscribers need all segment files of one video, and the URLs must not change. What do you use?
items.extra: Signed cookies give [access to multiple restricted files](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-signed-cookies-when-multiple-files-or-keep-urls), such as all files of an HLS video.

items.front: CloudFront Functions or Lambda@Edge: which one can make network calls?
items.extra: A Lambda@Edge function can [make network calls to external resources](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-lambda-edge-network-calls-allowed).

items.front: In CloudFront, files change with every release, and users must get the new versions. What does AWS recommend?
items.extra: [Versioning is less expensive](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-invalidation-prefer-versioning-for-frequent-updates) than invalidation, and it also controls copies in browsers.

items.front: In CloudFront, can the connection to an S3 website endpoint origin use HTTPS?
items.back: No. S3 website endpoints do not support HTTPS.
items.extra: With a website endpoint origin, [you can't configure CloudFront to use HTTPS](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-https-s3-website-no-https-to-origin) to the origin.

items.front: In CloudFront, can a distribution use an ACM certificate that you requested in eu-west-1?
items.back: No. Request it in US East (N. Virginia).
items.extra: To use an ACM certificate with CloudFront, you must request or import it in [US East (N. Virginia)](../facts/acm.md#acm-cloudfront-us-east-1).

items.front: Global Accelerator or a Route 53 failover record: which one does not depend on client DNS caches?
items.extra: With Global Accelerator you do not rely on [the IP address caching settings of client devices](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-no-dns-cache-dependency-seconds).

items.front: In CloudFront, do you pay for data transfer from an S3 origin to CloudFront?
items.back: No. It is free from AWS origins.
items.extra: Transfer from the origin to CloudFront is [always free when using AWS origins](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-price-origin-to-cloudfront-always-free-aws-origins). You pay for transfer out to viewers.

items.front: In CloudFront, cache policy or origin request policy: which one adds values to the cache key?
items.extra: A cache policy controls the values that are [included in the cache key](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-cache-policy-controls-cache-key).

items.front: In CloudFront, an internal Application Load Balancer in private subnets must be the origin. What do you create?
items.extra: CloudFront reaches [internal Application Load Balancers inside private subnets](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-alb-internal-needs-vpc-origins) through VPC origins.

items.front: In CloudFront, an internet-facing Application Load Balancer must accept CloudFront traffic and nothing else. What is the source of its security group rule?
items.back: The AWS-managed prefix list for CloudFront.
items.extra: As a best practice, allow inbound traffic from the [AWS-managed prefix list for CloudFront](../facts/elb.md#elb-alb-cloudfront-prefix-list-sg) and remove other inbound rules. To admit your own distribution alone, CloudFront can also [add a custom HTTP header to requests](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-alb-restrict-custom-header-and-https), and a listener rule checks it.

items.front: In CloudFront, can you use origin access control with an S3 website endpoint origin?
items.back: No. A website endpoint is a custom origin.
items.extra: A website endpoint is [also considered a custom origin](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-oac-s3-website-endpoint-not-supported), so [you can't use OAC (or OAI)](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-oac-s3-website-endpoint-not-supported).

items.front: In a CloudFront origin group, do POST requests fail over to the secondary origin?
items.back: No. CloudFront does not fail over POST requests.
items.extra: CloudFront fails over [only when the HTTP method of the viewer](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-failover-only-get-head-options) request is GET, HEAD or OPTIONS.

items.front: In Global Accelerator, does a traffic dial change close existing connections?
items.back: No. It applies to new connections.
items.extra: When you change a traffic dial, [the updated setting applies to only new connections](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-traffic-dial-new-connections-only).

items.front: In Global Accelerator, can an on-premises server be an endpoint directly?
items.back: No. Register a Network Load Balancer in a Region.
items.extra: You [can’t directly configure on-premises resources as endpoints](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-on-premises-via-nlb), but a Network Load Balancer can address them.

items.front: In Global Accelerator, Elastic IP address or accelerator static IP address: which one is advertised from AWS edge locations?
items.back: The Global Accelerator static IP address.
items.extra: Elastic IP addresses are [advertised from a single AWS Region](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-faq-vs-elastic-ip-scope-and-advertisement) at a time.

items.front: In CloudFront, viewers in many Regions overload one origin with cache misses. Which feature adds a central cache layer?
items.extra: Origin Shield is a [centralized caching layer](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-origin-shield-central-cache-layer) that reduces the load on your origin.

items.front: In CloudFront, can a viewer force a trip to the origin by sending Cache-Control: no-cache?
items.back: No. CloudFront ignores that header from viewers.
items.extra: [CloudFront ignores those header fields in viewer requests](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-expiration-viewer-cache-control-ignored).

items.front: In CloudFront, viewers in one country must not get any content of the distribution. What do you use?
items.extra: CloudFront answers a viewer in a restricted country with [403 (Forbidden)](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-faq-geo-restriction-403).

items.front: In CloudFront, which origin protocol policy encrypts the connection to a custom origin, whatever the viewer uses?
items.extra: With this policy, [CloudFront uses only HTTPS to access the origin](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-origin-protocol-https-only).

items.front: In Global Accelerator, a stateful application needs each user to reach the same endpoint. What do you set?
items.back: Client affinity by source IP address.
items.extra: For stateful applications, client affinity can [direct all requests from a user](../facts/global-accelerator.md#global-accelerator-client-affinity-for-stateful-apps) to the same endpoint.

items.front: In a CloudFront cache behavior, the default value of Default TTL is {{c1::86400 seconds}}.
In Global Accelerator, a new accelerator gets {{c1::two IPv4 static IP addresses}}.
In CloudFront, the {{c1::first 1,000 invalidation paths}} that you submit each month are free.
In Lambda@Edge, a function runs for {{c1::up to 30 seconds}}.
In CloudFront Functions, the maximum size of a function is {{c1::10 KB}}.
In Global Accelerator, an unhealthy endpoint is detected and taken out of service in {{c1::less than one minute}}.
In Global Accelerator, the default traffic dial of every endpoint group is {{c1::100%}}.
In a CloudFront origin group, connection attempts to an unreachable primary origin take {{c1::30 seconds}} by default before CloudFront tries the secondary origin.
items.extra: This number covers connection attempts. A primary that connects but does not answer also has a response timeout of [30 seconds](../facts/cloudfront.md#cloudfront-default-response-timeout) by default.
